overview: The two types of covalent bonds that make up single, double, and triple bonds — one forms along the bond axis, the other above and below it.
genZNote: Sigma bonds show up first and hold the fort. Pi bonds only join once there's already a sigma bond in place.

aspects.label: Orbital Overlap
aspects.valueA: Head-on (axial) overlap of orbitals along the internuclear axis.
aspects.valueB: Sideways (lateral) overlap of unhybridized p-orbitals, above and below the bond axis.

aspects.label: Relative Bond Strength
aspects.valueB: Weaker — less effective overlap than sigma bonds.

aspects.label: Free Rotation Around Bond?
aspects.valueA: Yes — a single sigma bond allows free rotation.
aspects.valueB: No — pi bonds restrict rotation, which is why double bonds are rigid (enabling cis-trans isomerism).

aspects.label: Occurrence
aspects.valueA: Present in every single, double, and triple bond (always the first bond formed).
aspects.valueB: Present only in double bonds (one π) and triple bonds (two π), never alone.
